chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man divorces his wife while she is pregnant, he must spend upon her until she gives birth to her child; and when she gives birth, he gives her her recompense (for breastfeeding), and he should not harm her, except if he finds someone who is cheaper in recompense than her. So if she is pleased with that recompense, she is more rightful with her son until she weans him.
ai.seo_question: What are the husband's financial and custody obligations when divorcing a pregnant wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the financial and custodial rights in a divorce involving a pregnant woman, emphasizing that maintenance continues until childbirth and breastfeeding compensation is due upon delivery. It establishes the mother's primary right to custody ('ahq') until weaning, contingent on her acceptance of the agreed recompense, while allowing the father to seek a cheaper alternative if he finds one. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'nafaqah' and 'ujrah' as distinct yet interconnected obligations ensuring the child's welfare and the mother's dignity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, form Muhammad Bin Al Fazeyl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man divorces his wife, and she is pregnant, he has to spend upon her until she places her burden (give birth); and when she has placed it, he has to give her, her recompense (for breast feeding), and he should not harm her except if he finds one who is cheaper in recompense than her. So if she is pleased with that recompense, so she would be more rightful with her son, until she weans him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘When a man divorces his wife, who is pregnant, he must provide her maintenance until she gives birth. When she gives birth he must pay her wages and must not harm her unless he finds someone who does it for less; but if she agrees with the lesser wages then she has more right to breastfeeding her child until the child is weaned.’”
